extracted.intended_audience: Organizations (universities, industry, non-profits, small businesses) preparing white papers, proposals, or full applications in response to ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B001
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation/administrative requirements for preparing and submitting white papers, technical and cost proposals, and full grant/contract applications to the Office of Naval Research under BAA N00014-23-S-B001. Covers evaluation process, compliance (export, human subjects, biosafety, security), subcontracting, proposal format, and award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of funds is a selection consideration (Not applicable to white papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per NDAA 2021 Section 1062 (effective Oct 1, 2024), DoD may not fund institutions of higher education that host a Confucius Institute (defined as a cultural institute directly or indirectly funded by the PRC) except amounts provided directly to students as education assistance, unless a waiver is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection is recommendation-based and contingent
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection/recommendation for award is made by ONR's scientific/technical community and forwarded to Contracts and Grant Awards Management; recommendation does not guarantee an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After recommendation, Contracting/Grants office conducts cost analysis, responsibility determination, confirms funds, and may require demonstration of compliance (e.g., enhanced cybersecurity) prior to award. Notification of recommendation must not be construed as authorization to expend funds; only a signed award by a Contracting or Grants Officer authorizes work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals not compared head-to-head
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other because they are not submitted to a common work statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR intends to review all proposals as soon as possible but may review periodically for administrative reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to small business participation (Contracts only)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR strongly commits to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities for small businesses and socio-economic categories (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs, HBCUs, minority institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers from contractors should maximize practicable opportunity for small business participation consistent with efficient performance; ONR provides resources (Apex Accelerators, DSBS, SAM.gov, SBA directories) to assist businesses unfamiliar with federal contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan requirement for contract proposals > $750,000
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits (including educational institutions) must provide a Subcontracting Plan containing all elements required by FAR 19.704, FAR 52.219-9, and DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are exempt. The Plan must be submitted as an attachment to the Proposal Checklist and will not count in page count. If an offeror has a Master/Individual or Comprehensive Subcontracting Plan, a copy should be attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan review and negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted Subcontracting Plans will be reviewed for adequacy to ensure required information, goals, and assurances are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR 19.702 requires an apparent successful offeror to submit an acceptable Plan; failure to negotiate a Plan acceptable to the contracting officer within the prescribed time makes the offeror ineligible for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business participation goals and SDB threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall propose realistic goals to ensure maximum practicable small business participation; if proposed goals have no positive goals or SDB goals are below 5%, include a viable written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation should describe why small businesses are unable to be utilized and what attempts were taken to provide opportunity. Plans should aim to include SDB participation; lack of positive goals requires justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting resources and outreach (FAR 5.206 notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities may post notices to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) to seek competition for subcontracts and increase small business participation under criteria in FAR 5.206.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices may be posted by (1) a contractor awarded a contract exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold likely to result in subcontracts, or (2) a subcontractor/supplier under a contract exceeding the threshold with a subcontracting opportunity exceeding $15,000. Notices must describe the business opportunity, prequalification requirements, and where to obtain technical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONR facilitation of subcontracting arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR will help facilitate prime contractor / small business connections by posting non-proprietary contact information of small businesses that indicate subcontracting interest and technological niche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses interested in subcontracting should email ONR Small Business Director with: company name/website; POC name and email; business size and socio-economic category; brief technology description (≤3 sentences, no marketing); technology keywords (≤10 words). Do NOT include proprietary information; information will be publicly posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of options for award purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Options will be evaluated by adding the total cost for all options to the total cost for the basic requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the options during performance. Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panel composition and confidentiality protections
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers and technical/cost proposals will be protected from unauthorized disclosure; evaluations performed by cognizant Program Officer and Government scientific experts; support contractors may be used for administrative or SME consultant purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and award decisions remain sole responsibility of Government personnel. Contractor employees with access must sign ONR NDA for Contractor Support prior to receipt of submissions; NDA includes third-party beneficiary language allowing submitter direct action against contractor/employer for NDA violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and award documentation process
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants receive email notification advising whether their proposal has been selected or not for recommendation for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants recommended for award may be contacted for additional information (representations/certifications, revised budgets, certificate of current cost or pricing data, subcontracting plan, etc.). Notification email is not an authorization to commit funds; only an award document signed by the Contracting/Grants Officer authorizes commencing the project. ONR award/modification documents are available via EDA in PIEE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors are responsible for complying with all U.S. export control laws/regulations (ITAR, EAR) and must address in proposals whether ITAR or EAR restrictions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must obtain any required licenses or approvals (or claim exemptions) for exports of hardware, technical data, software (including deemed exports), or provision of technical assistance. Refer applicants to ITAR/EAR regulations and Export Control Reform Initiative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification and need for classified access
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must identify any need for access to classified material in Section II, Block 11 of the Proposal Checklist; ONR will attempt to enable work at unclassified level where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified access is required, a DD Form 254 will be attached and FAR 52.204-2 Security Requirements incorporated into the contract. ONR does not provide access to classified material under grants or cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animals in research
rubrics_metrics.description: If animals are to be utilized, Offerors must comply with DoD policies (DoD Instruction 3216.01 and DHA-MSR 6025.02) and submit required documentation (Full or Abbreviated Appendix) with supporting documents (IACUC approval, approved protocol, USDA inspection report) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should contact ONR Animal Use Administrator for assistance and consult the provided guidance link for submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human subjects in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must protect rights/welfare of human subjects and comply with the Common Rule (DoD implementation at 32 CFR part 219), DoD Instruction 3216.02, SECNAVINST 3900.39E, 10 USC 980, and applicable FDA/federal/state laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to award, for proposals involving human subjects, provide IRB approval (protocol, consent, documentation showing IRB considered scientific merit), proof of human research training, institutional FWA (including suspensions/terminations), any exemption determinations with supporting documentation signed by IRB official, or determinations that activities do not constitute human subjects research. Documentation submitted via ONR Program Officer to ONR HRPO; HRPO has final judgment and must accept IRB approval/determination before research may commence. Government will not reimburse work performed in violation of this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with DODM 6055.18 Safety Standards for Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories and meet at least minimum applicable requirements of CDC BMBL, NIH Guidelines, and applicable FDA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional biosafety practices meet current editions and provide related documentation as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules (rDNA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must not begin performance of research within the scope of the NIH Guidelines until ONR has reviewed and accepted Offeror documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide (a) a written institutional statement of compliance with NIH Guidelines or applicable FDA requirements (on institutional letterhead, signed by an official other than the PI), and (b) evidence of IBC approval (or exemption) and DHHS Letter of Approval of the IBC (or most recent DHHS letter stating compliance). Contact ONR HRPO for assistance, especially for work outside U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and funding agencies subject to the USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences DURC must comply with all listed requirements for research involving certain biological agents or toxins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If research directly involves listed agents/toxins, contact the cognizant Technical POC. Refer to USG S3 guidance (S3/dualuse) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) access
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may be eligible for DoD HPCMP assets to support funded activities subject to ONR Program Officer approval and completion of security/screening requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult https://www.hpc.mil/ for additional information and coordinate with Program Officer for access approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Review and Program Review Meetings (expectations and cost estimating)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may hold Individual Project Review Meetings (about one day, typically two in-person per year) and Program Review Meetings (generally once per year, 2–3 days) to review results and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cost estimating, assume ~40% of review meetings at/near ONR Arlington VA and ~60% at other government or non-government facilities within continental U.S. Offerors may offer to host Program Review Meetings (include estimated cost and specified sample language); inclusion of hosting language is optional and will not affect selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on procurement of foreign-made Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: COTS UAS may not be purchased pursuant to this award for prototype until a waiver per Deputy Secretary memorandum (May 23, 2018) is obtained by the cognizant ONR Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: waiver not required when research is via a grant award that is unclassified, funded with basic (6.1) or applied (6.2) research funds, and performed on campus by a university. Waiver required for other grants/assistance, for efforts involving interactions with military personnel/DoD property/DoD facilities/US Government labs/UARCs/FFRDCs/PAO/classified or specific military utility. For contract awards and OTAs, waiver required and Cyber Security waiver or ATO and Cyber Vulnerability Assessment must be obtained. Prospective/current performers must notify ONR Program Officer of anticipated COTS UAS purchases at white paper/proposal submission or award changes and must provide supporting documentation; performers must cooperate to support the waiver and assessment. No federal funds may be expended for purchase until waiver and cyber vulnerability requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting requirements differ by award instrument; see Appendix 1 for Grants/Cooperative Agreements/TIAs and Appendix 2 for Contracts and OTAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific reporting schedules and content in the applicable appendix for the award type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and question handling (unclassified and classified)
rubrics_metrics.description: All UNCLASSIFIED communications must be submitted via email to the Technical POC with a copy to Business POC. CLASSIFIED questions must be handled through ONR Security POC via an UNCLASSIFIED email requesting to ask a CLASSIFIED question; do not email classified questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical, business, grants, and security contacts with email/address details are provided for appropriate inquiries. Questions of technical nature should go to the POC for the appropriate technology area; international offerors to contact ONR Global Science Director as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal file format and attachment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Files attached to mandatory forms must be PDF, must not contain macros, and must not be password protected; non-conforming attachments will be rejected by automated acceptance check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions must be marked 'New' in SF 424 block 2. Electronic file names must not exceed 68 characters including extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal formatting: font, spacing, and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Proposal formatting: single spaced; Times New Roman font no smaller than 12-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss page limits for the Technical Proposal with the cognizant Program Officer. There are no page limitations for the Budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 (R&R) and mandatory forms completion specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete mandatory SF-424 Research and Related forms per form instructions and specific field guidance in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special instructions include: Field 3 leave blank; Field 4a Federal Identifier enter N00014 for new proposals; Field 4b Agency Routing Number format: three-digit Program Office Code and Program Officer's name (e.g., '331 [Smith, John]'), pad two-digit codes with a '0' after code (e.g., Code 31 -> 310); use Code 600 for ONRG. Failure to provide Program Officer Code may result in rejection. Field 5, 11, 14, 16, 17, and 19 have additional instructions in the solicitation (certifications, authorized representative email, inclusion of ONR White Paper Tracking Number in title if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project summary/abstract must identify the research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only standard QWERTY characters; spell out Greek/other symbols; graphics are not allowed; one page or 4,000-character limit (whichever is less). Do not include proprietary/confidential information. The abstract must be marked 'Approved for Public Release'. Abstracts of funded projects will be posted publicly on DTIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Other Project Information fields and Project Narrative attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete R&R Other Project Information fields for human subjects (Fields 1/1a), vertebrate animal use (Fields 2/2a), environmental compliance (Fields 4a-4d), and attach the entire technical proposal as the Project Narrative in Field 8 as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field 7 (Project Summary/Abstract) leave blank and complete SF424 Project Abstract instead; if system error prevents leaving blank, upload the Project Abstract. Project Narrative must describe research objectives and approach, organized in the sections described in solicitation, and be attached as a single PDF named 'Technical Proposal'. The technical proposal must include a cover page with: BAA number, proposal title, identity of prime offeror and list of subawards, technical contact info, and administrative/business contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental compliance field guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Fields 4a-4d to indicate whether intended research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory and how compliance with environmental statutes/regulations will be ensured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal awards must comply with environmental planning/regulatory requirements (e.g., NEPA). Many ONR-funded field research activities may be categorically excluded, but questions should be referred to the technical point of contact.
